scopeReview: SPS-3.A.3–4: socially constructed changing practices, urbanization/globalization, media/technology/politics/economics/social ties, time–space convergence, language-domain pressure and cultural convergence/divergence. English/international-language roles treated contextually without current unverified rankings.
varietyReview: Communication line chart, local/global network model, shared-platform/content table and language-upload bars. Other applied cases address uneven access, promotion, language domains, digital local expression, local adaptation, sampling and reciprocal ties. All five skills and mixed difficulty/keys.
repetitionReview: Contemporary channels distinguish the set from3.5 historical institutional/trade causes. Time delay is not migration distance; common platform and varied content are different dimensions; production counts do not estimate language vitality. No repeated stems or numeric-only clones.
referenceNote: Official scope and primary institutional context for digital language diversity/access checked. Hypothetical platforms, communities and numbers only; no company algorithm facts, copied datasets, external catalog imports or human-review claims.

questions.correctOption: Delivery falls from 48 hours to 30 minutes, reducing the time barrier without changing physical distance.
questions.independentReview: Independently converted0.5×60=30 minutes and compared48/0.5=96 as a delivery-time ratio. Constant1000km prevents inference of physical shrinkage; no universal access claim follows.

questions.correctOption: Urban contact can reshape a practice locally, while digital networks amplify it across larger scales.
questions.independentReview: Traced R/S district contacts→city studio→international audience. Distinguished creation/adaptation from circulation and avoided claiming that audience reach establishes identical adoption or meaning.

questions.correctOption: A common technology can coexist with different language-content patterns.
questions.independentReview: Verified platform90/90 alongside R/S80/20 versus20/80, each post-language pair totaling100. Did not mix resident and post denominators or infer every individual’s language from aggregate content.

questions.correctOption: Uploads increased eightfold, but the chart does not measure changes in speaker numbers or proficiency.
questions.independentReview: Independently computed40/5=8 and40−5=35. Counts are uploads during equal periods, not users or speakers; repeated uploads by one creator are possible.

questions.correctOption: Faster networks can expand interaction while access remains unequal across people and places.
questions.independentReview: Separated network performance from household coverage. The supplied rural gap limits universal claims without negating the measured improvements or treating offline communities as culturally absent.

questions.correctOption: Commercial and technological decisions can shape which cultural expressions receive repeated exposure.
questions.independentReview: Distinguished controlled exposure channels from deterministic cultural outcomes. The hypothetical platform mechanism is supplied explicitly; no unverified claim about a real company’s algorithm is made.

questions.correctOption: Institutional incentives and global connections can expand one language’s use while putting pressure on another’s domains.
questions.independentReview: Tracked institutional domain shifts rather than equating language learning with immediate replacement. The scenario permits pressure, bilingualism and responses; no real language’s current status is invented.

questions.correctOption: A global channel can also support local expression and cultural divergence.
questions.independentReview: Separated the platform’s scale from the cultural specificity of its content. A possible divergence/revitalization channel is supported without asserting guaranteed language survival.

questions.correctOption: Global connections can produce locally modified expressions rather than one identical product everywhere.
questions.independentReview: Compared organizational integration with variable menu content. No named company, real dietary rule or historical ingredient-origin claim is supplied.

questions.correctOption: The platform sample may omit relevant populations and cannot automatically represent all regions.
questions.independentReview: Identified coverage bias rather than merely sample size. The policy conclusion exceeds the urban connected sampling frame; no particular rural preference is assumed.

questions.correctOption: Contemporary networks can support reciprocal, multi-scale cultural change rather than one-way copying.
questions.independentReview: Traced city→origin adaptation→city feedback as reciprocal connections. Distinguished content transmission from population relocation and avoided a single dominant-source assumption.
